notes:
Technical description of the accepted tree; it sets no deployment policy. Supply split, allocations, owners and chain come from the separately versioned launch policy.

TOKEN: LaunchToken (src/LaunchToken.sol), OpenZeppelin ERC20 v5.1.0, name 'Launch Guard', symbol GUARD, 18 decimals. Zero-argument constructor mints exactly 1,000,000,000 GUARD (10^27 minor units) once to msg.sender, the factory. No owner, mint, burn, pause, tax, proxy or selfdestruct.

HOOK: LaunchGuardHook (src/LaunchGuardHook.sol) extends the vendored v4-periphery BaseHook; solc 0.8.26, evm cancun, via_ir, optimizer 200 runs, bytecode_hash none. getHookPermissions returns exactly beforeInitialize and beforeSwap (address flags 0x2080 = 8320); the other twelve flags, including all four return deltas, are false, so liquidity changes and donations never reach the hook and it never returns a delta or overrides the LP fee. BaseHook restricts both callbacks to the PoolManager. No owner, setter, pause, upgrade, exemption or custody; the hook never holds funds or calls unlock, swap, take or settle.

CONSTRUCTOR (IPoolManager manager, IERC20 token): argument 0 is the launch chain's PoolManager, written as $poolManager. The constructor requires manager code and a nonzero token address, then fixes launchToken immutably. Token code and totalSupply() are checked during the first successful beforeInitialize callback, which stores maxBuyAmount = totalSupply / 100 = 10,000,000 GUARD. Failed initialization rolls back this value.

UNRESOLVED DEPLOYMENT BLOCKER: constructorArgs[1] is the literal zero address, so this manifest cannot deploy LaunchGuardHook: its constructor reverts InvalidConfiguration. Zero is not a substitution marker; '$token' is unsupported. A valid literal can be predicted using the actual factory and token salt/init-code hash (CREATE2) or factory nonce (CREATE). Neither those deployment inputs nor a verified LaunchToken address are supplied. Replace argument 1 with that verified address before deployment; guessing would bind the wrong token. The hook now permits a nonzero future token address without code at construction, addressing the separate fresh-EVM admission issue. Token code must exist there before initialization. Notes cannot substitute addresses or authorize interface changes.

BEHAVIOUR: beforeInitialize reverts InvalidPool for a pool that does not name this hook or does not contain the launch token, AlreadyInitialized for a repeated PoolId, then records guardEndsAt[poolId] = block.timestamp + 86,400 s and emits GuardStarted. beforeSwap reverts PoolNotInitialized for an unknown PoolId. While block.timestamp < guardEndsAt it reverts BuyLimitExceeded(10,000,000 GUARD) for any swap whose output currency is the launch token and whose output would exceed 1% of total supply: an exact-input or above-cap exact-output request whose previewed actual output exceeds the cap (src/libraries/SwapPreview.sol reproduces core SwapMath, tick traversal, LP and protocol fees and the trader's price limit from live PoolManager state). Exactly the cap is allowed. Sells, partial fills within the cap, liquidity changes and donations are never restricted; from guardEndsAt onward every swap passes. Per-swap limit only: several swaps, even in one transaction, can buy more in aggregate. The preview is read-only; its gas grows with crossed ticks.

POOL: currency0 native ETH, currency1 GUARD, static LP fee 3000 (0.3%), tickSpacing 60. initialPrice 79299443975792720780679863727831 is TickMath.getSqrtPriceAtTick(138180), about 1,001,800 GUARD per ETH (about 998 ETH fully diluted); the source fixes no price, so this tick-aligned value is chosen here and the factory seeds one-sided GUARD liquidity below it. The 24-hour guard starts at the factory's initialize call. The CREATE2 salt is mined per deployer and init code for flags 0x2080.

Local checks do not establish the missing deployment address or resolve the constructor blocker.
